validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, federally docketed project -- not a GEM-only entity. CE FLNG, LLC filed a DOE/FE application on September 21, 2012 (Docket No. 12-123-LNG) and received FTA export authorization (DOE/FE Order No. 3193, Nov 21, 2012, 8 mtpa/30-year term). FERC approved a pre-filing environmental review request (Docket No. PF13-11-000) in early 2013 for a combined LNG terminal + pipeline project by 'CE FLNG, LLC and CE Pipeline, LLC' -- confirmed independently by Natural Gas Intelligence (Apr 22, 2013, an affiliate of Cambridge Energy Holding LLC) and by FERC's own Notice of Intent to prepare an EIS (Federal Register 2013-29600, Dec 12, 2013). CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as a gas transmission lateral, not a gathering/distribution line -- the FR NOI describes 'approximately 37 miles of 42-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana' feeding the CE FLNG floating LNG terminal on the Mississippi River (river mile marker ~12.5, northeast of Venice), i.e. a dedicated LNG-feed transmission lateral. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of, or the same physical project as, any other PID in this 44-row Gulf Coast roster -- no other row references Plaquemines Parish river-mile-12.5/Venice, the CE FLNG/Cambridge Energy sponsor, or Docket PF13-11/12-123-LNG; this is unrelated to Venture Global's separate Plaquemines LNG/Gator Express project (different sponsor, different site, different docket family) despite the similar 'Plaquemines LNG' search noise. CAVEAT: the pipeline never advanced past FERC's pre-filing stage -- FERC terminated the pre-filing environmental review on October 11, 2016 'due to lack of progress' and closed the administrative record (per DOE's Jan 17, 2025 Notice of Dismissal, which takes administrative notice of FERC's 2016 letter), and CE FLNG has not re-initiated a FERC pre-filing review in the 8+ years since. See status_reviews for the recommended Status change.

Both entities are affiliates of Cambridge Energy Holding LLC / Cambridge Energy LLC, so this is a within-family correction (pipeline-specific SPV vs. terminal SPV), not a change of ultimate sponsor.

status_reviews.staleness_rule: n/a -- confirmed discrete regulatory inactivity, not a dormancy inference

verifications.note: DOE, Jan 17, 2025: 'on October 11, 2016, FERC issued a letter to CE FLNG terminating its pre-filing environmental review process for the proposed Project and closing the administrative record due to lack of progress. ... more than eight years have passed since FERC issued the termination notice, yet CE FLNG has not initiated a new pre-filing review process with FERC.' Also: 'The only filing by CE FLNG in its docket since June 2013 was a "Docket Service List Update" filed in January 2023.' DOE goes on to dismiss the pending non-FTA portion of CE FLNG's 2012 export application WITHOUT PREJUDICE (CE FLNG may refile), leaving the 2012 FTA export authorization nominally in place.

Cambridge Energy's own website (Wayback capture, Apr 17, 2024): 'Cambridge Acquisition Corp ... is a Canadian integrated hydrogen to power company that is transitioning from LNG and developing a hydrogen power platform business that is focused on de-carbonization and providing carbon free power' -- lists 'LNG project development of US LNG Export projects (CE FLNG)' as past activity (2008-2013 era experience), with the company 'now focused on ensuring H2 Power' -- independent confirmation the sponsor is no longer actively pursuing the LNG project.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=proposed is stale and should change to shelved (not cancelled -- DOE's dismissal is explicitly 'without prejudice' and the 2012 FTA export authorization remains nominally in force; CE FLNG's own Oct 2024 semi-annual DOE filing still frames the project as 'delayed'/'TBD' and describes ongoing, if minimal, efforts ('working through issues', 'evaluating the impact of market changes', 'identify[ing] new LNG Supply Agreement(s)') rather than an affirmative withdrawal or cancellation -- this is a real but indefinitely-paused project, matching 'shelved' rather than 'cancelled' in the controlled vocabulary). Two independent origins meet the corroboration bar: DOE's own Jan 2025 legal order (citing FERC's 2016 termination letter and the applicant's own admissions) and Cambridge Energy's own current corporate website (a separate, independently-fetched source, not merely restating the DOE record) confirming the parent company has moved on to a hydrogen-power business. ShelvedYear is set to 2016, the year FERC terminated the pre-filing environmental review 'due to lack of progress' -- the clearest documented inflection point after which the project made no further forward progress (the only subsequent docket activity in nearly 12 years was a purely administrative 'Docket Service List Update' in January 2023). ShelvedCancelledType='confirmed' rather than 'inferred' because this rests on DOE's own sourced account of a discrete FERC action and the applicant's own admissions, not a GEM dormancy inference from silence. evidence_date is set to 2025-01, the date of the most recent independent dated evidence found (DOE's Notice of Dismissal); the Cambridge Energy website capture (2024-04) is the second-most-recent. Note for a future researcher: under the sweep's own dormancy rule ('shelved >=4y -> cancelled'), a project shelved since 2016 could arguably already be graded 'cancelled' rather than 'shelved' -- left at 'shelved' here because DOE's own 2025 characterization ('without prejudice', still accepting semi-annual reports, FTA authorization not revoked) is more precise, current, sourced evidence than applying the blanket dormancy rule over sourced evidence would be.
